newsitem.title: USA: Florida extends high speed rail deadline.
newsitem.headline: Florida extends high speed rail deadline.

text.p: Backers of a futuristic high speed rail network have been given an extra two weeks to come up with a plan to pay for the $5 billion project, state transportation officials announced late Wednesday.

Florida Overland eXpress, the Orlando-based consortium chosen this spring to build the Miami-Orlando-Tampa network, was given until Nov. 12 to come up with a financially viable package. Otherwise the deal is off.

"We have made significant progress with FOX on some extremely complex financial negotiations," Florida Secretary of Transportation Ben Watts said in a statement. FOX really has stepped up and become a true partner with us on this project."
The extension marked the second time in less than three months that FOX was granted more time to sew up loose ends. Company officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
In August, state officials gave FOX 90 days to to amend its original proposal to move passengers from Miami to Orlando to Tampa in less than 2 1/2 hours.
The state, which has pledged $70 million a year to help finance the project, wanted FOX to bring more to the table.

Specifically, the August agreement called for the company to come up with $300 million in federal funds over six years to help build a system expected to be completed by 2006. In addition, the company needed to seek a federal guarantee for revenue bonds to be repaid by ticket sales.

The 90-day extension was scheduled to end Oct. 31. On Wednesday, Watts said negotiations with FOX had proceeded favorably and offers of help from Florida's Congressional delegation and the U.S. Department of Transportation convinced him to extend the deadline.

So far, financing has been the biggest stumbling block, but earlier this week state officials received encouraging news from the U.S. Department of Transportation. Federal assistance has been deemed essential to the project's success.

"This administration stands ready to assist you in tailoring your financial plan so as to maximize your potential for gaining the financial aid so necessary for this important project," Deputy Secretary Mortimer Downey told Watts in a letter received Monday. In particular, we hope to be able to work with you as we develop proposed innovative financing methods, including federal credit enhancement opportunities."
